methods.label: Cancel consecutive factors
methods.explanation:
The consecutive triangular numbers suggest looking for factors that cancel between neighboring terms. Adding \(1+2+\cdots+k\) to the same sum in reverse order gives \(k\) pairs, each totaling \(k+1\). Hence
\[
T_k=\frac{k(k+1)}2.
\]
For every integer \(k\ge2\),
\[
\frac{T_k}{T_k-1}
=\frac{k(k+1)}{k(k+1)-2}
=\frac{k}{k-1}\cdot\frac{k+1}{k+2}.
\]
All denominators here are positive. Splitting the product into these two chains exposes the cancellation:
\[
P_n=
\left(\prod_{k=2}^{n}\frac{k}{k-1}\right)
\left(\prod_{k=2}^{n}\frac{k+1}{k+2}\right).
\]
In the first chain, the factors from \(2\) through \(n-1\) cancel, leaving \(n\). In the second, the factors from \(4\) through \(n+1\) cancel, leaving \(3/(n+2)\). These endpoint formulas also hold when \(n=2\), when there are no internal factors to cancel. Thus
\[
P_n=\frac{3n}{n+2}.
\]
In particular,
\[
P_{1991}=\frac{5973}{1993}
=3-\frac6{1993}.
\]
Since \(0<6/1993<0.1\), this value lies between \(2.9\) and \(3\). It is less than \(0.1\) from \(2.9\), more than \(0.2\) from \(3.2\), and farther from every smaller choice than from \(2.9\). The closest number is \(\boxed{2.9}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
